name: LZ
summary: LZ uses a multitonne dual-phase xenon target at SURF's 4850-foot level in the United States to search for dark matter, building on LUX and the UK's ZEPLIN experience.
detection_principle: Xenon S1/S2 signals measure recoil energy and three-dimensional position. An external liquid-scintillator detector and other vetoes reject radioactive and neutron backgrounds.

results.summary: The extended high-energy nuclear-recoil search observed one nuclear-recoil candidate in a region with low expected background. Statistical significance is insufficient for a discovery claim; it must not be described as detection of dark matter.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
